scenarios.title: Find a subnet’s block size
scenarios.summary: Read a prefix and mask, calculate a block size and locate an address.
scenarios.objective: For 192.168.50.146/27, complete the native subnet worksheet. Use the given prefix to determine the requested values; reserve network and broadcast in this conventional exercise.
steps: Complete the whole worksheet and check your reasoning.

guide.title: Apply the method
guide.why: A mask determines equally sized groups of addresses.
guide.action: Use the labeled worksheet. Introduction and separate practice remain available.

scenarios.explanation: The subnet mask fixes network bits. Subtract the relevant mask octet from 256; round down to a boundary. Later host octets run from 0 to 255. The next subnet follows the entire block; broadcast is one address before it.
hints: Find the mask value at the last network bit.
Block size = 256 minus that mask value; find the boundary at or below the relevant IP octet.
Network uses all-zero host bits; broadcast uses all-one host bits. Reserve both for this exercise.
scenarios.simplifications: Conventional IPv4 broadcast subnets /1–/30. /31 point-to-point and /32 host routes are special cases outside these worksheets; subtracting two is not universal. Native mathematics only, no packet or device simulation.
